beliefs.practice: Use a single long-lived MongoClient (pymongo.MongoClient) per process and reuse it across requests; do not create a new client for each request. Configure connection pooling (maxPoolSize) appropriate to your concurrency.

Never commit the cluster connection string or keys to source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any keys) from environment variables or a secrets store and never log them. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead of the real secret.

Use role-based, least-privilege credentials where possible (short-lived tokens / managed identity or service principal). If using a connection string, scope it to a user with only the needed database/collection privileges rather than the admin/master key.

Store each text chunk as a separate document with explicit metadata fields: source_id (pubmed_id), source_year, chunk_index, chunk_text, original_doc_id, and embedding vector in a dedicated field named embedding (array of floats). This enables citations and year filtering without parsing text.
Keep documents small (well under 16MB) by chunking long abstracts and storing only one chunk per document; use a deterministic chunk_id so you can re-assemble or dedupe chunks later.

Choose a chunk size tuned to your embedding model (e.g., ~512 tokens per chunk with 10–20% overlap) and validate empirically that retrieval quality vs. cost is acceptable. Store chunk length and token count in metadata for debugging.

When ingesting many documents, use batched bulk writes (insert_many or bulk_write) with moderate batch sizes (e.g., 500–2000 docs per batch) and ordered=False to maximize throughput and continue on partial failures.

Create a native vector index that matches your embedding dimensionality and similarity metric (cosine/dot/Euclidean) and explicitly set the index type (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and parameters (e.g., efConstruction, M or index-specific settings) to optimize search latencies and recall.

Include metadata fields you will filter on (pubmed_id, source_year) in the same collection and create regular (B-tree) indexes on them so vector k-NN results can be pre-filtered server-side efficiently.

When running vector similarity queries, prefer server-side vector search operators (native k-NN) rather than scanning embeddings client-side, to reduce network and CPU cost and take advantage of the DiskANN/HNSW index.

Ensure the stored embedding vectors use the precision expected by the index (typically float32). Avoid converting to strings or nested documents; store vectors as a flat numeric array in the embedding field.

When you call vector search, request top-k results and include the document metadata (pubmed_id, year, chunk_index) in projection so each hit can be returned with grounded citations; also persist the original text snippet so the app can display evidence without an extra fetch.

Use retries with exponential backoff for transient network / rate-limit errors. Prefer the driver's built-in retryWrites/retryReads when available and add application-level backoff for idempotent operations (ingest, index creation, queries).

When creating indexes or loading large datasets, perform those operations off-peak or in a maintenance window and monitor RU/IO usage; index builds can be resource intensive and affect query latency and billing.

Avoid N+1 reads: design queries to fetch the vector search results and required metadata in one DB query or use projection to include text and citation fields rather than issuing a separate lookup per hit.

Create conventional indexes on any fields you query for filtering and sorting (e.g., source_year descending) and verify index usage with explain() or the platform's query plan tooling; remove unused indexes to reduce write costs.

Record provenance and citation metadata (PubMed ID, year, PMID URL, ingestion timestamp) with each chunk. Use these fields for deterministic citation formatting in the RAG responses rather than embedding metadata only in application memory.

Secure the cluster with network controls: restrict allowed client IPs or use VNet service endpoints/private endpoints; enable TLS for client connections and validate server certificates in the client driver.

Instrument and monitor vector index health and query performance (latency, recall metrics) and sample explain plans for vector queries; log coarse metrics (queries/sec, average k-NN latency, RU consumption) to detect regressions after model or index changes.

For local dev and CI tests, include a minimal, non-secret .env.example and mock or skip external LLM/embedding API calls during automated tests; provide integration steps in README for the full pipeline that require secrets.
When upgrading or altering vector indexes (changing metric / dimensionality), reindex all stored embeddings or store the embedding model version with each document to detect mismatch at query time.

If cost is a concern, consider quantizing or compressing embeddings offline (e.g., float32->float16 or product quantization) but validate compatibility with the server-side vector index (some native indexes require float32 arrays).

Use explain() or the cluster's inspection tools (the provided documentdb MCP tools) to validate that created indexes (including the vector index) are active and that queries use them; verify result ordering and relevance on representative queries.

Limit fields returned by queries using projection to reduce network egress (e.g., only return chunk_text, pubmed_id, source_year, score) and avoid returning full embeddings unless needed for downstream processing.
